description: Columbia AI Toolkit (formerly CHAT) offers institutional model access. At CUIMC, Sensitive Data/PHI approval depends on the approved model and account; every model sharing the chat history must be approved. The captured August2026 footnote limits PHI-approved Toolkit models to OpenAI models. Access is not assessment permission.
howToObtain: Sign in with Columbia UNI at aitoolkit.cuit.columbia.edu
costToUser: Free baseline daily allowance ($0.15/day); departmental funding for higher usage

evidence.evidenceSnippet: **Importantly, for students:** Faculty retain primary responsibility for determining whether and how AI is used in their courses. In conjunction with departmental and curricular guidelines, faculty may authorize or prohibit the use of AI in preparing academic work on a course-by-course basis. Please confirm with your instructor before using AI for any academic purpose.

✓* - CUIMC users of CU AI Toolkit are approved to use Sensitive Data (PHI) provided it is used with approved AI models. By default, CUIMC members are restricted to AI models approved for PHI data (currently OpenAI models within CU AI Toolkit). As of August 2026, only the OpenAI models in CU AI Toolkit are approved for use with sensitive data. Dual-Affiliates may have expanded access and should be aware that the full chat history is visible to all models used in a chat. Do not input Sensitive Data unless all models used in the chat are approved for use with Sensitive Data. CUIMC Dual-Affiliates and non-CUIMC CU AI Toolkit users should not input PHI data unless all models in CU AI Toolkit are
approved for use with PHI data. For any questions, contact the CUIMC IT AI Working Group at 5help@cumc.columbia.edu.

description: Institutionally provisioned ChatGPT Edu with enterprise privacy; conversations/data are not used to train OpenAI models. Sensitive Data use depends on the current CUIMC account, model and feature approvals; do not infer universal permission or a blanket BAA from access alone. Live Web Search restrictions must be checked separately.
howToObtain: Departmental request through CUIT or CUIMC IT provisioning
costToUser: $300 annually per user UNI via departmental chart string

evidence.evidenceSnippet: ChatGPT Edu, available to the Columbia University community, offers enterprise-grade security and data privacy (conversations and data are not used to train OpenAI models), along with access to OpenAI's latest models.

description: OpenAI ChatGPT enterprise access for CUIMC clinical workforce with HIPAA data protections (verify on-screen logo). Note: Clinical clearance is distinct from coursework rules.
howToObtain: Sign in with CUIMC credentials; verify on-screen Columbia logo indicator
costToUser: Enterprise-provisioned for eligible workforce and clinical members

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
Draft or summarize clinical documentation only inside PHI-approved tools using your CUIMC account.

- Verify the on-screen approval indicator where applicable before entering any patient data.

- Treat AI output as a draft — clinicians remain responsible for accuracy.

description: LionMail Google Workspace Gemini access is distinct from CUIMC Google Enterprise/GCP provisioning. Workspace has no Columbia HIPAA BAA for Sensitive Data. Apply stricter handling where FERPA data includes identifying or health information; tool access is not assessment permission.
howToObtain: Log in to Google Workspace using Columbia LionMail credentials
costToUser: Free to all active university Google Workspace account holders

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Standard Google Gemini is available for the majority of users who have access to Lionmail at no additional costs.

Google Gemini/Gemini Notebook in Google Workspace (CUIT) is not approved for Sensitive Data, while the Enterprise editions in GCP (CUIMC IT) are — a direct illustration of the HIPAA difference explained above.

description: Anthropic Claude for Education offering enterprise security and institutional controls for sponsored members ($300/yr). Note: IT clearance is not course assessment permission. The captured CUIMC guidance limits Claude to non-sensitive data; institutional access does not override data classifications.
costToUser: $300 annually per user UNI via departmental chart string

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Claude for Education is now available to the Columbia University community. Claude is an AI assistant created by Anthropic that helps you think, write, code, and solve problems. You can use Claude for teaching, learning, research, and administrative work across the university. The Education offering provides enhanced security, privacy, and institutional controls. Users have access to Anthropic’s latest Claude models, along with advanced analysis tools, file handling, image capabilities, and web search.
Columbia ChatGPT Education, CU AI Toolkit, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Claude — non-sensitive data only.

description: At CUIMC the captured August2026 approvals cover Copilot Chat, M365 Copilot and Copilot in Microsoft Fabric; Copilot Studio and GitHub Copilot in VSCode are not approved for Sensitive Data. Use the approved account/product and current controls; CUIT M365 access is a separate provision, not assessment permission.
howToObtain: Log in with CUIMC account at copilot.microsoft.com; CUIT M365 support request
costToUser: Provided for CUIMC clinical workforce; available as paid add-on for CUIT M365 customers

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Microsoft Copilot is not currently a supported AI tool by CUIT for the Columbia Community. If you are currently a CUIT supported [M365 service](https://www.cuit.columbia.edu/microsoft-365) customer, Copilot is available as an "add-on", and is supported by the M365 support team. If you are a CUIMC community member, please reach out to [CUIMC IT](https://www.it.cuimc.columbia.edu/about-us/contact-us) for more information about Copilot.

† Microsoft CoPilot is an overarching brand that covers several separately licensed Microsoft AI products. As of August 2026, CUIMC-approved HIPAA-compliant products include CoPilot Chat, M365 CoPilot (integrated into M365 “Office” suite), and CoPilot in Microsoft Fabric. At this time, any other Copilot products such as CoPilot Studio and GitHub Copilot in VSCode are not approved for use with sensitive data.

description: Gemini Notebook/NotebookLM within institutional Google Workspace. Workspace sensitive-data restrictions and FERPA identifying/health overlaps apply; institutional access does not grant general data or assessment permission.
howToObtain: Access via Columbia Google Workspace credentials

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) is now available to the Columbia University community. This AI-powered research and note-taking assistant helps you organize, summarize, and synthesize information from your own documents and trusted sources.

Google Gemini/Gemini Notebook in Google Workspace (CUIT) is not approved for Sensitive Data, while the Enterprise editions in GCP (CUIMC IT) are — a direct illustration of the HIPAA difference explained above.
